q: Alice owns deploy.sh, but running it says Permission denied. Is the fix chmod 777 or chmod u+x?
expl: Only the execute bit was missing. Seven seven seven would let every user on the system change the script.

q: Which mode lets only the owner read and write a password file?
expl: Six hundred: read and write for the owner, nothing for the group or anyone else.
ch: Problem 2: a secret anyone can read

q: `ls -l` shows `-rw-r--r-- 1 alice web 6 index.html`. What may members of the group `web` do with the file?
expl: The middle three letters `r--` belong to the group: read, no write, no execute.
opts: Nothing, only alice may open it

q: `deploy.sh` starts as `-rw-r--r--` (644). What does this print?
expl: Owner gets x (rwx = 7), the group gets x (r-x = 5), others stay read-only (r-- = 4). Removing write that isn't there changes nothing.

q: Type a `chmod` command for the folder `private`: full access for the owner, the group may list and enter it, everyone else gets nothing.
expl: `750` = rwx for the owner, r-x for the group, nothing for others. Starting from 755, `o-rwx` gives the same result.

q: The folder `private` has mode 744 (`drwxr--r--`). Can a member of its group read `private/notes.txt`?
expl: On a folder, `r` lets you list the names and `x` lets you go inside. Opening a file in it needs `x`.
opts: Yes, `r` on the folder is enough
No: without `x` the group can't enter the folder

q: You "fix" a Permission denied on `index.html` with `chmod 777`. What is the real problem with that?
expl: The last 7 gives everyone read, write and execute. Bob, who has nothing to do with the site, can replace the page.
ch: Why chmod 777 is a bad fix
opts: Only root can read the file afterwards
Every user on the system, like bob, can now overwrite the file
Nothing, 777 only adds the execute bit

q: Type a `find` command that lists the regular files (`-type f`) in the current folder that everyone (others) can write.
expl: `-perm -o=w` means “at least the write bit for others”. Without the dash, find wants exactly that mode and finds nothing.
ch: Why chmod 777 is a bad fix

q: `index.html` belongs to `alice:root`. Type one command that makes bob the owner and `web` the group.
expl: `chown user:group file` changes both at once; with only a user name, the group stays as it was.

q: Alice owns `index.html`. Can she give it to bob with `chown bob index.html`?
expl: Only root may change a file's owner, so on a normal system you put sudo in front of chown.
opts: Yes, the owner may give her files away
Yes, if bob is in the same group
No: changing the owner needs root, which is why you'd use sudo
